name: Jet Pilot
description: Three rums, falernum, cinnamon and grapefruit with a drop of absinthe — a Zombie descendant built to be even harder to reverse-engineer.
funFact: Tiki bars deliberately obscured their recipes — Don the Beachcomber numbered his mixes and had staff work from coded bottles so nobody could copy them, including his own bartenders.

steps: Add every ingredient to a blender with a cup of crushed ice.
Flash-blend for about five seconds — do not liquefy it.
Pour unstrained into a double rocks glass.
Top with more crushed ice to fill.
Garnish with a mint sprig.

name: Test Pilot
description: Don the Beachcomber's rum-and-falernum formula with Cointreau and Angostura. Complex, dry and considerably stronger than it tastes.
funFact: Also called the Missionary's Downfall in some bars, though that is properly a different drink — tiki recipe names were reused and misattributed constantly.

steps: Combine all ingredients in a shaker with crushed ice.
Shake hard for 10 seconds.
Pour unstrained into a tiki mug or coupe.
Add crushed ice to fill if needed.
Garnish with a cherry and a mint sprig.

name: Doctor Funk
description: Rum, absinthe, lemon and grenadine over soda — named for a real doctor who practised in Samoa and prescribed something similar.
funFact: Dr Bernard Funk was a German physician in Samoa who treated Robert Louis Stevenson; his absinthe-and-lemonade remedy became a South Pacific drink long before tiki bars adopted it.

steps: Shake everything except the soda with ice.
Pour into a highball glass packed with crushed ice.
Top with soda water.
Stir gently once with a swizzle stick.
Garnish with a mint sprig and a lime wheel.

name: Cobra's Fang
description: Demerara rum with falernum, orange, lime and a lash of absinthe. Spiced, bitter-edged and one of the sharper Beachcomber formulas.
funFact: Falernum, a Barbadian lime-clove-almond syrup, is the single most tiki ingredient there is — it appears in more Beachcomber recipes than any spirit except rum.

steps: Shake all ingredients with crushed ice for 10 seconds.
Pour unstrained into a tiki mug.
Top with fresh crushed ice.
Garnish with a lime wheel and mint.
Serve with a straw.

name: Missionary's Downfall
description: Blended with fresh mint, peach and pineapple — bright green, herbaceous and the least brown drink in the tiki canon.
funFact: Most tiki drinks are variations on rum, citrus and spice; this one is essentially a frozen mint julep with fruit, and it stands out on any tiki menu for that reason.

steps: Put the mint, pineapple and lime juice in a blender.
Add the rum, peach brandy and honey syrup.
Add crushed ice and blend until smooth and pale green.
Pour into a chilled coupe.
Garnish with a mint sprig.

name: Nui Nui
description: Gold rum with vanilla, cinnamon and allspice over orange and lime. The spice cabinet of tiki in one glass.
funFact: Beachcomber's spice syrups were mixed in advance and labelled only with numbers — 'Don's Spices #2' is allspice and vanilla, and the code was cracked decades later by tiki archaeologists.

steps: Shake all ingredients with crushed ice for 10 seconds.
Pour unstrained into a tiki mug.
Top with crushed ice.
Garnish with an orange twist and a cinnamon stick.
Serve with a straw.

name: Pearl Diver
description: Three rums whipped with a butter-and-spice 'gardenia mix' — the only classic cocktail that calls for butter as a core ingredient.
funFact: The gardenia mix — butter, honey, cinnamon and allspice creamed together — is what makes it work; it emulsifies into the drink and gives a richness nothing else achieves.

steps: Make the gardenia mix by creaming softened butter with honey, cinnamon and allspice.
Add a spoonful to a blender with the rums, juices and crushed ice.
Flash-blend for five seconds until emulsified.
Pour into a tall glass and top with crushed ice.
Garnish with a mint sprig.

name: Royal Hawaiian
description: Gin, pineapple, lemon and orgeat from the pink hotel on Waikiki — the rare tiki-era drink built on gin rather than rum.
funFact: The Royal Hawaiian hotel opened in 1927 and is still called the Pink Palace of the Pacific; its bar predates the mainland tiki craze by a decade.

steps: Shake all ingredients hard with ice for 12 seconds.
Double-strain into a chilled coupe.
Garnish with a pineapple wedge.
Serve immediately.

name: Halekulani
description: Gin, lemon, orange and grenadine with bitters — the house drink of a Waikiki hotel, sharper and less sweet than its neighbours.
funFact: The Halekulani's House Without a Key bar has served it since the 1930s under a century-old kiawe tree that still stands on the terrace.

steps: Shake all ingredients hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe or over fresh ice.
Garnish with an orange slice and a cherry.
Serve cold.

name: Beachcomber
description: A Daiquiri with triple sec and maraschino — the drink Don the Beachcomber named himself after, and simpler than anything else he made.
funFact: Ernest Gantt legally changed his name to Donn Beach after the bar became famous — the man took his identity from the restaurant rather than the other way round.

steps: Shake all ingredients hard with ice for 12 seconds.
Double-strain into a chilled coupe.
Garnish with a lime wheel.
Serve immediately.

name: Chief Lapu Lapu
description: A rum punch scaled up and named for the Filipino chief who killed Magellan. Served in a hollowed pineapple where possible.
funFact: Lapulapu defeated Magellan at the Battle of Mactan in 1521 and is a national hero in the Philippines, which makes his appearance on a Los Angeles tiki menu somewhat unexpected.

steps: Shake all ingredients with ice for 10 seconds.
Pour unstrained into a hollowed pineapple or a large tiki mug.
Top with crushed ice.
Garnish extravagantly with fruit and mint.
Serve with long straws, ideally shared.

name: Shrunken Skull
description: Two rums, lime and grenadine over crushed ice in a skull mug. Short, tart and considerably less complicated than its neighbours.
funFact: Tiki mug collecting is now a serious market, and vintage skull mugs from mid-century Los Angeles bars change hands for hundreds of dollars.

steps: Shake all ingredients with ice for 10 seconds.
Pour unstrained into a skull mug.
Top with crushed ice.
Garnish with a lime wheel.
Serve with a straw.

name: Port Light
description: Bourbon, passionfruit, lemon and honey shaken with egg white — a tiki drink built on whiskey, which almost none of them are.
funFact: Its bourbon base makes it an outlier in a category defined by rum, and it is one of the few tiki drinks that works as well in winter as in summer.

steps: Dry-shake all ingredients without ice for 15 seconds.
Add ice and shake hard for 15 seconds more.
Pour into a hurricane glass over crushed ice.
Garnish with a lemon wheel and a cherry.
Serve with a straw.

name: Blue Hawaiian
description: A Piña Colada turned blue with curaçao. Distinct from the Blue Hawaii, which has vodka and no coconut — a difference nobody enforces.
funFact: Harry Yee, at the Hilton Hawaiian Village, created the original Blue Hawaii in 1957 at the request of a blue-curaçao sales representative — the drink existed to sell an ingredient.

steps: Add all ingredients to a blender with ice.
Blend until smooth and pale blue.
Pour into a hurricane glass.
Garnish with a pineapple wedge and a cherry.
Serve with a straw and a paper umbrella.

name: Chi Chi
description: A Piña Colada made with vodka instead of rum. Cleaner, less funky, and the version ordered by people who say they dislike rum.
funFact: The swap is the entire recipe — everything else matches a Piña Colada — and it exists mostly because vodka outsold rum in the 1970s American market.

steps: Add all ingredients to a blender with ice.
Blend until completely smooth.
Pour into a hurricane glass.
Garnish with a pineapple wedge and cherry.
Serve with a straw.

name: Bahama Breeze
description: Coconut rum, banana and pineapple with a dark rum float — the resort blender drink refined into something with actual structure.
funFact: The dark rum float is the difference between a fruit smoothie and a cocktail — it hits the nose first and reframes everything underneath it.

steps: Shake the coconut rum, banana liqueur, pineapple and lime with ice.
Strain into a hurricane glass over fresh ice.
Float the dark rum over the back of a spoon.
Garnish with a pineapple wedge.
Serve with a straw.

name: Rum Barrel
description: A multi-rum punch served in a barrel-shaped mug, closer to a scaled-up Zombie than to anything restrained.
funFact: Barrel mugs, skull mugs and hollowed pineapples were part of the same commercial logic — the vessel was the marketing, and customers frequently stole them.

steps: Combine everything in a shaker with crushed ice.
Shake for 10 seconds.
Pour unstrained into a barrel mug.
Top with crushed ice.
Garnish with mint and a cherry.

name: Aku Aku
description: Light rum blended with peach, mint and pineapple — pale, fresh and named for Thor Heyerdahl's book about Easter Island.
funFact: Heyerdahl's 'Aku-Aku' was a 1957 bestseller about Easter Island, and tiki bars borrowed Polynesian book titles as freely as they borrowed everything else.

steps: Put the mint in a blender with the lime juice and press briefly.
Add the rum, peach liqueur, pineapple juice and syrup.
Add crushed ice and flash-blend for five seconds.
Pour into a tiki mug.
Garnish with a mint sprig and a pineapple wedge.

name: Sidewinder's Fang
description: A large, spice-heavy rum and citrus punch, traditionally served with a coil of orange peel arranged to look like a snake.
funFact: The garnish is the name: a long spiral of orange peel draped over the rim, which the bar staff cut in one continuous piece as a small display of knife work.

steps: Shake everything but the soda with crushed ice.
Pour unstrained into a large tiki mug.
Top with soda and more crushed ice.
Cut a long spiral of orange peel and drape it over the rim.
Serve with a straw.

name: Molokai Mule
description: Rum, ginger, orange and lime — the tiki answer to a Moscow Mule, spiced rather than sharp.
funFact: Ginger runs through tiki from falernum to Doctor Funk; the mule format simply gives it the lead instead of a supporting role.

steps: Shake the rum, ginger syrup and juices with ice.
Pour into a mug packed with crushed ice.
Top with soda water.
Stir once with a swizzle stick.
Garnish with candied ginger and a lime wheel.

name: Puka Punch
description: Four rums, honey, passionfruit and grapefruit, served long over crushed ice. One of the heaviest pours in the canon.
funFact: The Tiki-Ti bar in Los Angeles has served it since 1961, and the staff ring a bell and shout when one is ordered — a ritual that has outlasted most of the tiki era.

steps: Shake everything except the overproof rum with crushed ice.
Pour unstrained into a large tiki mug.
Top with crushed ice.
Float the overproof rum over the top.
Garnish with mint and a cherry.

name: Tahitian Rum Punch
description: Rhum with lime, grenadine and tropical juice, poured long — the French Polynesian take on a punch, lighter than its American imitations.
funFact: Tahiti gave tiki bars their aesthetic vocabulary and almost none of their recipes — the actual drinking culture of French Polynesia runs to rhum, beer and fruit juice.

steps: Shake all ingredients with ice for 10 seconds.
Pour into a highball glass over fresh ice.
Stir once to bring the grenadine through.
Garnish with a lime wheel and a flower if you have one.
Serve with a straw.

name: Hukilau
description: Rum with passionfruit, lime and a dry curaçao — named for the communal net-fishing that ends with everyone eating on the beach.
funFact: A hukilau is a Hawaiian group fishing method where the whole village hauls a single net; the song about it was a mainland hit in 1948 and the drink followed the song.

steps: Shake all ingredients with crushed ice for 10 seconds.
Pour unstrained into a tiki mug.
Top with crushed ice.
Garnish with a lime wheel and mint.
Serve with a straw.

name: Vicious Virgin
description: Two rums, falernum, curaçao and lime — a short, dry Beachcomber formula with none of the fruit-juice padding of later tiki.
funFact: The early Beachcomber drinks were markedly drier and stronger than the tiki of the 1960s; the sweetening happened later, as the format spread to restaurants that wanted volume.

steps: Shake all ingredients with crushed ice for 10 seconds.
Pour unstrained into a small tiki mug or coupe.
Add crushed ice to fill.
Garnish with a lime wheel.
Serve immediately.

name: Shark's Tooth
description: Demerara rum with lemon, grenadine and soda — a long, red, deceptively simple drink from the same kitchen as the Zombie.
funFact: Donn Beach built dozens of recipes from the same handful of syrups; the difference between many of his drinks is a quarter-ounce of one ingredient, which is exactly what made them hard to copy.

steps: Shake everything except the soda with ice.
Pour into a tall glass packed with crushed ice.
Top with soda water.
Stir once with a swizzle stick.
Garnish with a lime wheel and a cherry.

name: Cradle of Life
description: Rum, lime, honey and a cinnamon-spiced syrup with a whole egg — one of very few tiki drinks built on an egg.
funFact: Tiki almost never used eggs, which makes this an outlier — the egg gives it a texture closer to a flip than to a punch.

steps: Dry-shake all ingredients without ice for 20 seconds.
Add ice and shake hard for another 15 seconds.
Double-strain into a chilled coupe.
Dust with grated cinnamon.
Serve immediately.
